Hello everybody,

I just committed some code to github that should fix the problems.

- The warning was indeed because somewhere in the code there was a hard coded "3" that should be #lags+1
- The error is caused by underdetermined linear systems. lm then gives NAs that lead to errors later. My solution is to use ginv instead of lm. Hopefully, this doesn't cause trouble elsewhere.

@Matthieu: I sent you a pull request in github..

>> On the other side, I observe a very strange behavior I cannot understand...
>> library(tsDyn)
>> library(FinTS)
>> a<-coredata(m.unrate)
>>
>> star(a[1:400]) #ok
>> star(a[1:500]) # returns strange object???
>>

This seems odd, but I think it is correct. At the beginning of the star function, a test for linearity is performed, which detects that a[1:400] is non-linear, but a[1:500] is linear. Therefore, no fitting is performed for a[1:500] (maybe it would be better to directly fit an AR then, as it is done by ncstar).

This seems not to be a problem of the star function, but of the theory behind it. You can try:

library(fNonlinear)
tnnTest(a[1:400])
tnnTest(a[1:500])

to see that also the implementation of the test in the fNonlinear package yields this result..

Regards,
Christoph

doing to do it...), so a try-catch solution is probably the best :-)

On 05/14/2011 09:38 AM, mat wrote:
> thanks for these explanations Antonio! I guess that these problems arise while doing the grid search Christoph (this is case for me in TVECM) ? Then
> indeed it should be possible to ban the value in question with NA, instead of trying to return something in any case... well maybe for some later work

Mat, thanks for also having a look into this. What you say is true. However, I think that in theory the problem should not be too much of an issue,
because what ginv does is just picking one solution of the infinitely many ones. In practice, of course there went probably wrong something else
before (badly chosen values in the grid search, a degenerated time series,...). So what we could do is: use lm, and if there are NAs, then give a
warning and return the result of ginv.

>
> Christoph, Josï¿½: Indeed I feel would be nice to return linear model instead of just the data! (just data is quite surprising for user)
>
> This would involve just:
> if(!increase) {
> if(trace) cat("The series is linear. Use linear model instead.\n")
> return(str);
> }
>
> to
> if(!increase) {
> if(trace) cat("The series is linear. Use linear model instead.\n")
> return(linear(str, m=m));
> }
>
> I can do the changes if you want? Just let me know what you think of it?

It might be more convenient to return a star object (with only one regime) that contains the linear model, instead of directly the linear model. But
for now I think this is an easy and good solution, so feel free to commit the change..

Regards,
Christoph
